precepts.text: Blessed is the man that doth meditate good things in wisdom, and that reasoneth of holy things by his understanding. When we do not study, we have nothing in our spirits to combat Satan; we are defenseless. Even Christ, when he was tempted, used the word of God: is it not written? When you meditate good things, you can reason in the scriptures: wait, the scripture says this; I cannot do that. When you go before the magistrates, think not what ye shall say; but you have to have something in your spirit for the Lord to work with. If you have no scriptures about lust in your head, where are you going to pull from? Give the Holy Spirit something to work with. When Joseph was tempted, he referred straight back to the law: I would be sinning against God. That was what came to his mind first, because his mind was always on the scriptures.
precepts.point: Wherefore, my dearly beloved, flee from idolatry. Why is idolatry the word here? Because you idolize these temptations. That appetite, the lust within you, becomes an idol to you: you idolize that demon inside of you and you feed it, and it is never enough.

note.label: Satan's Kiss To Your Demise

precepts.why:
“There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able”. The Lord still gives you enough strength not to be overtaken, and always a way out. But it is up to you. Sometimes we are weak in the faith and weak in the spirit: you don't read your four chapters a day, your conversation is not about the scriptures, you are not around the brothers, and Satan gets a hold of you.

When we do not study, we have nothing in our spirits to combat Satan; we are defenseless. Even Christ, when he was tempted, used the word of God: as it is written. We have to be the same way. Sirach: “Blessed is the man that doth meditate good things in wisdom, and that reasoneth of holy things by his understanding.”

When you meditate on good things, you can reason in the scriptures in the moment of temptation: wait, the scripture says this; I can't do that. “He that considereth her ways in his heart” is always asking, what does the scripture say about this? That is how you combat the lust, the demon: you have to have something in your spirit.

When you go before the magistrates you are told not to think about what you will say, but you still have to have something in your spirit for the Lord to work with. If you have no scriptures about lust in your head, where are you going to pull from? Give the Holy Spirit something to work with. When Joseph, our forefather in Egypt, was tempted, he went straight back to the law: I would be sinning against God. That came to his mind first because his mind was always on the scriptures. Temptation always comes with an exit; addiction forms when we stop taking the exit.

precepts.text: He made him to hear his voice, and brought him into the dark cloud, and gave him commandments before his face, even the law of life and knowledge, that he might teach Jacob his covenants, and Israel his judgments. The baptism unto Moses goes back to the commandments, because that represents Christ.
precepts.point: To summarize: Israel needed manna every day to survive the wilderness, and Christ compared that to needing the word of God. I am not saying simply read your Bible. The point is that spiritual life requires consistent, continual nourishment, just as physical life requires continual food. Those of you who think you are ten toes down: when Jacob's trouble magnifies itself, you are going to survive that with this diet? You need to be training all the time for that day. Be the warrior in the garden instead of a gardener in a war. There is a big difference between trials and tribulation; the scripture says we have not yet resisted unto blood.

note.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

precepts.why:
“Moreover, brethren, I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea”. Everybody says the Corinthians were Gentiles. If they were Gentiles, how is it that all their fathers were under the cloud in the wilderness? Reading is fundamental; sometimes it is as simple as that.

“And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea”. When they try to tell you what baptized means, go to Sirach: “He made him to hear his voice, and brought him into the dark cloud, and gave him commandments before his face, even the law of life and knowledge, that he might teach Jacob his covenants, and Israel his judgments.” That is Moses being given the commandments in the cloud.

The baptism is the receiving of the laws and the doing of the laws, in the faith of Christ; do not leave that part out, because the whole Bible is about Christ. Moses did not dip the six hundred thousand men and all the rest into rivers. Where was the water? The Lord had to provide water from a rock. It all goes back to the commandments, because that represents Christ.

Then “did all eat the same spiritual meat”: the manna, and the law of life and knowledge. “And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.” Everything in the wilderness was the foreshadowing, the setup, to show the dependency we would need on Christ. Many were overthrown in the wilderness, not by an enemy but by their own lusts, and the way to avoid lusting after those things is to feed yourself on the word of God daily.

precepts.text: The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ? For we being many are one bread, and one body: for we are all partakers of that one bread. We are all partakers of that manna.
precepts.point: He took bread, and gave thanks, and brake it, and gave unto them, saying, This is my body which is given for you: this do in remembrance of me.

note.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

precepts.why:
Christ “took bread, and gave thanks, and brake it”, and said, “This is my body which is given for you”. Paul shows what that breaking of bread is: “The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ?”

“For we being many are one bread, and one body: for we are all partakers of that one bread.” We are all partakers of that manna. Christ is the true manna, the bread from heaven, and we feed upon Christ through his words.

So when we break bread together we are not only eating a piece of bread. We are showing that we are one body, all of us feeding on the same bread, which is Christ and the word of God. That is the fuller sense of “this do in remembrance of me.”

precepts.text: I led my people out of Egypt, and brought him up to mount Sinai, where I held him by me a long season: the forty days and forty nights. He told Moses many wondrous things and showed him the secrets of the times, the beginning, the middle, and the end; that is how Moses wrote the first five books, and how he saw even his own end before the promised land.
precepts.point: All these things happened unto them for ensamples, and are written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come. The acts of the apostles continue; we are learning from our forefathers the same way the congregations in Asia Minor did.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
“And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea”. That baptism is Moses teaching us the laws of God, and teaching us the gospel, teaching us about Christ, because Moses spoke with Christ. Christ said, “Before Abraham was, I am”: it was Christ that spoke directly to Moses. We often think the gospel only begins in the book of Matthew. It does not.

Ezra shows it: “And I sent him and led my people out of Egypt, and brought him up to the mount of where I held him by me a long season”. That mount is Sinai, and the long season is the forty days and forty nights. “And told him many wondrous things, and shewed him the secrets of the times, and the end”.

Moses was shown the beginning, the middle and the end of times; that is how he was able to write about it in the first five books. He even saw himself not entering the promised land. “These words shalt thou declare, and these shalt thou hide.”

“That thou lay up in thy heart the signs that I have shewed, and the dreams that thou hast seen, and the interpretations which thou hast heard: For thou shalt be taken away from all, and from henceforth thou shalt remain with my Son, and with such as be like thee, until the times be ended.”

So when Paul says our fathers “did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ”, it is plain: the Israelites in the wilderness were taught the gospel through Moses, who had been with Christ on the mount. Those things are written “for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come”; we learn from our forefathers the same way the congregations scattered in Asia Minor did, and the acts of the apostles continue.

precepts.text: Ye cannot drink the cup of the Lord, and the cup of devils. You cannot do both. If you're doing both, you're lukewarm, and the Lord said he'd rather you hot or cold; the lukewarm are not getting the kingdom.
precepts.point: There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape. The Lord will give you a way to escape: this book, beholding your face in the glass, and the people he sends into your life to instruct you. But some hear that and say, I don't want to escape; I want to stay in this same place, and still say I believe in God. Does that work? No.

note.label: Pay The Price: Pleasure Now Regret Later

precepts.why:
“Wherefore let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall.” A man is wise in his own eyes; take heed, walk circumspectly. “but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape”. The Lord gives you a way to escape: this book, where you behold your face in the glass, and the people he sends into your life to instruct you and show you change.

But some hear it and say, I know the Lord is giving me a way to escape, but I don't want to escape. I want to stay in this same place, and still say I believe in God. Does that work? No.

Paul answers it a few verses later: “Ye cannot drink the cup of the Lord, and the cup of devils: ye cannot be partakers of the Lord’s table, and of the table of devils.” You cannot do both. “I speak as to wise men; judge ye what I say.” Judge it by what we just read: you cannot have it both ways. You have to choose one.

If you are doing both, you are lukewarm, and the Lord said he would rather you were hot or cold. Don't play the middle ground. If you are cold you are not getting the kingdom, and if you are lukewarm you are not getting the kingdom either, so why be lukewarm? “Wherefore, my dearly beloved, flee from idolatry”: whatever your god is, flee from it and take the way of escape he gives.

precepts.text: These things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted. Why were they overthrown in the wilderness? Because they lusted after evil things. Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them committed, and fell in one day three and twenty thousand. The rose up to play was fornication, and it destroyed us. The nations understood this when they took their crafty counsel.
precepts.point: The people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play. That rose up to play was not hopscotch.

note.label: Pay The Price: Pleasure Now Regret Later

precepts.why:
At the golden calf “the people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play.” What was that rose up to play? You think it was hopscotch? Paul explains it.

“Neither be ye idolaters, as were some of them; as it is written, The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.” He is quoting the very verse, and before it he says: “Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted.” When they lusted after evil things, that is the rose up to play.

The verse before that: “But with many of them God was not well pleased: for they were overthrown in the wilderness.” Why were they overthrown in the wilderness? Because they lusted after evil things.

Then verse 8: “Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them committed, and fell in one day three and twenty thousand.” So we understand the rose up to play was fornication. They lusted after evil things, and it destroyed us.

The nations understood this. When we are in sin, they know what will happen, they can destroy us. So when they took their crafty counsel they said, how do we keep these people in error? They like to rap, so give them murder music and lascivious music. That is why they give our sisters these songs, so vulgar. Their whole plan is to keep us in sin. Pleasure now, regret later: you are going to pay.

precepts.text: How that all our fathers were under the cloud: right here it tells you who the people in Corinth are. They were not Greeks or Europeans; they were Israelites: our fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Under the cloud: the chariot that followed us. They drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them, and that Rock was Christ. But with many of them God was not well pleased, for they were overthrown in the wilderness: for murmuring, gossiping, fornication. These things were our examples, that we should not lust after evil things as they also lusted.
precepts.point: Even as Sodom and Gomorrha, giving themselves over to fornication, and going after strange flesh: other nations, and worse, as it is today. They are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire: that lake of fire we read about in Revelation 14.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
Jude says “I will therefore put you in remembrance, though ye once knew this, how that the Lord, having saved the people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed them that believed not.” He is going into history. When we left Egypt we went into the wilderness, and the Israelites rebelled and were put to death. Who else spoke of it in the New Testament? Paul, in Corinthians the tenth chapter. Write that down in your Bible.

“Moreover, brethren, I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud”. Right here it tells you who the people in Corinth were. They weren't white people, weren't Europeans, weren't natural Greeks, Caucasians. They were Israelites: our fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, not Abraham, Isaac and Esau. Under the cloud: the chariot that followed us. They “all passed through the sea; And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea”, because Moses taught the law and taught us Christ, the gospel.

“And did all eat the same spiritual meat; And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.” Christ was always present. “But with many of them God was not well pleased: for they were overthrown in the wilderness”: for murmuring, gossiping, sex, fornication.

“Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted.” These things were our examples, brothers. That is what Jude puts us in remembrance of: God saved a whole people and still destroyed those who believed not. Don't lust after evil things as they did, and earnestly contend for the faith once delivered unto the saints.

precepts.text: There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: if we see a spirit here, as leaders we have to understand that spirit is elsewhere. But God is faithful, and will with the temptation also make a way to escape. What is the way to escape? Put a class on. Call a brother; speak to your brother, to get that spirit off of you. A lot of times the devil jumps on us and we start battling in our own mind and create a whole other reality that does not even exist. You talk to the brother and realize all that mess you were thinking and rehearsing is not even the case.
precepts.point: There is one body, and one Spirit: what is going on here is going on elsewhere. The Lord puts the spirit on the leadership to bring out the class that addresses the prevalent issue at the time. We are dealing with bitterness in the midst of Passover, and the Lord reveals it is not just here but throughout the congregations.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
“There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man.” Bitterness is a very common thing that many of us battle with. We are never alone in it: if leadership sees a spirit in one congregation, they have to understand that the same spirit is elsewhere. That is the “one body, and one Spirit” of Ephesians 4:4. The classes are not rehearsed, yet the same talking points come out in different places, because the Lord puts the spirit on the leadership to address the prevalent issue of the time, and in the midst of Passover He revealed bitterness throughout the congregations.

“But God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.” Even while being tried and tempted, the Lord in His faithfulness makes a way out.

What is the way to escape? Put a class on. Call a brother. Speak to your brother, to get that spirit off of you. A lot of times the devil jumps on us and we start battling in our own mind, and we create a whole other reality that does not even exist in real life. You talk to the brother and you say, damn, all that mess I was thinking and rehearsing is not even the case.

That matters, because bitterness is the hidden leaven that must be purged. If it is not purged, it grows into a root that defiles the soul. Many brothers who left the body and came out with crazy videos started with a root of bitterness.

precepts.text: All our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea. Paul is speaking to the Corinthians: if they all passed through the sea, that means the Corinthians were Israel, because no Egyptians passed through the sea. And the mixed multitude that came out died in the wilderness. Baptized unto Moses means Moses taught us God's laws. They drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ. Who was following us in the wilderness? Christ. Who killed the Egyptians? Christ.
precepts.point: The waters returned and covered the chariots and the horsemen: there remained not so much as one of them. Thus the Lord saved Israel that day out of the hand of the Egyptians, and Israel saw the Egyptians dead upon the sea shore. And the people feared the Lord, and believed the Lord, and his servant Moses. We celebrated Passover.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
Exodus 14 is one of the wars of the Lord: the Lord fought for Israel, overthrew the Egyptians in the midst of the sea, and “there remained not so much as one of them.” Paul looks back on the same crossing: “Moreover, brethren, I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea”.

That cloud is a chariot. And who is Paul speaking to? The Corinthians. If all their fathers passed through the sea, then the Corinthians were Israel. Did the Egyptians pass through the sea? No. And some will say there was a mixed multitude; the mixed multitude came out lusting after evil things and all died in the wilderness. If the wicked of our own people did not make it, what about the mixed multitude?

“And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea”: baptized unto Moses means Moses taught us; he taught us God's laws. “And did all eat the same spiritual meat; And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.”

Who was following us in the wilderness? Christ. Who killed the Egyptians? Christ. The Lord who fought for Israel at the Red Sea, the one Moses wrote of, was always Christ, and he is the one who will come back and smite spiritual Egypt, the land we live in today.

precepts.text: The sun to rule by day, the moon and stars by night, him that smote Egypt in their firstborn, brought out Israel with a strong hand, divided the Red Sea, overthrew Pharaoh, led his people through the wilderness, and smote great kings: for his mercy endureth forever. He killed our enemies because he had mercy on us, and we saw all of it and still do evil. There is no temptation that should derail us from the wide place, because his mercies endure forever.
precepts.point: There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man; God will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able, but will with the temptation make a way to escape. If you understand the joy of the elect you embrace the temptation, because he has your back. He wants you to make it, though there are those appointed to die. Nobody wanted to pay a landlord who tripled the rent in Brooklyn after counting heads across the street; that trial forced us to pool the real estate, carpentry, plumbing, and electrical talent the Lord had among us, and then he blessed us with the building in New York despite the detractors. We never took our eyes off the prize. Do not let anyone take your crown.

note.label: The Divine Orchestration and Purpose of the People You Encounter

precepts.why:
Paul says God “will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape”. There is no temptation that should derail us from inheriting the wide place, the kingdom that sits within the narrow passage (2 Esdras 7), because God's mercies endure for ever. David shows that mercy: “The sun to rule by day: for his mercy endureth for ever: The moon and stars to rule by night: for his mercy endureth for ever.” The Lord declared the end from the beginning and created all of this. We acknowledge his greatness and his mercy, and we tap into that comfort under the shadow of his wings.

“To him that smote Egypt in their firstborn: for his mercy endureth for ever: And brought out Israel from among them”. The Most High killed our enemies for us because he had mercy on us. We cried in Egypt, the Lord heard our cries and said, go down, Moses, tell Pharaoh to let my people go, or I will kill his firstborn.

“With a strong hand, and with a stretched out arm”, “To him which divided the Red sea into parts”, “And made Israel to pass through the midst of it”, “But overthrew Pharaoh and his host in the Red sea”, “To him which led his people through the wilderness”, “To him which smote great kings: for his mercy endureth for ever”.

We saw all of this, and we still get here today and do evil, just as our fathers under the cloud did. The Most High is trying to set us back up, but he wants to make sure we are in the right spiritual posture to inherit the kingdom. He lets us use his Bible as spiritual weapons to fight off the evil temptations so we can get to the wide.

It is of the Lord's mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not; they are new every morning. The Lord is my portion. We ask forgiveness in the Lord's prayer and he gives it, and we keep playing with sin.

note.label: The Divine Orchestration and Purpose of the People You Encounter

precepts.why:
Paul says the things that happened to our fathers “are written for our admonition”. Jeremiah shows how we hold on to them: “My soul hath them still in remembrance, and is humbled in me.” The them is the afflictions and punishments we are supposed to remember for breaking God's commandments in the past, and we are humbled because of it.

“This I recall to my mind, therefore have I hope. It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.” Do you hear that? That is the love the Lord has for us, his mercy enduring for ever. He loves you, sisters; he loves you, brothers. His compassions and his mercies fail not.

“They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.” His mercies are renewed every day, forgiving us. We say the Lord's prayer, we ask the Lord for mercy and to forgive our transgressions, and he does it. And we are still playing with sin.

“The Lord is my portion, saith my soul; therefore will I hope in him.” So now we are in the posture where he has given us a way to escape the evil all around us.

precepts.text: Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies. The table is the Bible. Habakkuk 2:2, write the vision and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it; Isaiah 30:8, write it before them in a table and note it in a book for the time to come, that this is a rebellious people. We read the tables about what is happening overseas as entertainment while our own spirit is rotten. You are in the greatest place on earth, being taught the future out of these pages, and some of you scorn it.
precepts.point: There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man; God will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able, but will with the temptation make a way to escape. If you understand the joy of the elect you embrace the temptation, because he has your back. He wants you to make it, though there are those appointed to die. Nobody wanted to pay a landlord who tripled the rent in Brooklyn after counting heads across the street; that trial forced us to pool the real estate, carpentry, plumbing, and electrical talent the Lord had among us, and then he blessed us with the building in New York despite the detractors. We never took our eyes off the prize. Do not let anyone take your crown.

note.label: The Divine Orchestration and Purpose of the People You Encounter

precepts.why:
God will with the temptation “make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.” While we endure the encounters of temptation that are common to us all, even the temptations of our own lusts, the Lord prepares a table for us: “Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over.” Why? Because his mercies endure for ever.

The table is the Bible. Habakkuk shows it: “Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables”. Isaiah shows it: “write it before them in a table, and note it in a book”. The tables are what we are supposed to be reading.

But we read the tables and talk about what's going on overseas while our own spirit is rotten. We read it like entertainment instead of changing what is really going on in us.

Brothers and sisters, you are in the greatest place on the planet earth, and some of you don't even realize it. You are getting teaching that tells you what is happening in the future, because we know the future from reading the Bible. And some of you play games, scorn what is brought out, and take this for a joke. The table is prepared in the presence of our enemies; eat from it.

The Lord told the prophet Habakkuk: since you want to get out of captivity, write the vision down, and make it plain upon the tables. That is what we are supposed to be reading.

Make it plain “that he may run that readeth it”: when we bring this out, everybody is going to be running, and we are going to run to teach it. The Bible is going to turn this whole system upside down: these are they which have turned the world upside down. But we have to be in it like that, not reading about overseas like entertainment while our own spirit is rotten.

precepts.why:
Paul says what happened to our fathers is “written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come.” Isaiah shows why it was written: “Now go, write it before them in a table, and note it in a book, that it may be for the time to come for ever and ever”.

This is to the wicked Israelites, us, our people. Go write it before them in a table, and put a note in the book about their wickedness, our wickedness, “that it may be for the time to come”: for today.

And it goes on: “That this is a rebellious people”. That is what is going on with our people; our people are rebellious. But the Bible is here to correct you and straighten you out. If you want it, there is a way for you to get it.

Those who refuse to learn from the past by reading it are doomed to repeat it. You will repeat it because you refuse to learn, and the same spirits will follow you and attach themselves to you, the way people move to a new town, a new job or a new congregation and the same problem follows. The Lord sends those spirits as a mirror to show you what is wrong in you. Learn it from the book, and you won't have to learn it again.

precepts.text: Thou shalt have no other gods before me, nor make any graven image, nor bow down to them. Celebrating Valentine's Day puts Februus and Lupercalia before the Lord.
precepts.point: The Lord gave us our own high holy days in Leviticus 23. The Destruction of Nicanor, recorded in 1 Maccabees 7 and 2 Maccabees 14 and 15, began last night at sundown, and Purim, our deliverance from Haman through Esther and Mordecai, begins tonight. Our enemies' holidays are victories over us; ours are victories over them.

note.label: Prepare Ye War

precepts.why:
“Wherefore, my dearly beloved, flee from idolatry”. That is in the New Testament, for you black Christians, you black apologists, you black pastors who say the law is done away with. Why would Paul write it if the law was done away? Because it goes right back to Exodus 20: “Thou shalt have no other gods before me”.

“Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth: Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me”. That is where 1 Corinthians 10:14 comes from.

Valentine's Day is idolatry; its origin is Februus and Lupercalia, a fertility rite in which women presented themselves to be struck because it was believed to help with fertility. When you sit up there and celebrate Valentine's Day, you are putting Februus, whoever the hell that is, and Lupercalia before the Lord. What's wrong with Christmas? It's idolatry. Your birthday? Idolatry. Halloween? Idolatry. That's what's wrong with it.

The Lord gave us our own high holy days, in Leviticus 23. The Destruction of Nicanor began last night at sundown, the victory recorded in 1 Maccabees 7 and 2 Maccabees 14 and 15, when Judas Maccabeus defeated and killed Nicanor, the Seleucid Syrian Greek commander who came to crush Israel and threaten the temple. Tonight at sundown begins Purim, when we were saved from being wiped out in the Persian Empire: the enemy was Haman, and the deliverance came through Esther and Mordecai. Our enemies' holidays, the Fourth of July and Christmas, are victories over us. Ours are victories over our enemies. Flee from their idolatry and keep what the Lord gave us.

precepts.text: Wherefore, my dearly beloved, flee from idolatry.
precepts.point: The worshipping of idols not to be named is the beginning, the cause, and the end of all evil. Idolatry is your stubbornness, your bullheadedness, and your disdain for God's commandments.

note.label: The Iranians & The Ephesians

precepts.why:
“For the worshipping of idols not to be named is the beginning, the cause, and the end, of all evil.” Understand that idolatry is not only bowing to a statue. Idolatry is going into your stubbornness, your bullheadedness, and your disdain for God’s commandments. Setting your own will above the commandments is the beginning, the cause and the end of all evil.

So Paul gives the answer to it: “Wherefore, my dearly beloved, flee from idolatry.” Do what? Flee from idolatry. Do not stand there and bargain with it; run from it.

This comes as the Lord promises to gather his people: “I will save my people from the east country, and from the west country”, and bring them to dwell in the midst of Jerusalem, “and they shall be my people, and I will be their God, in truth and in righteousness.” The twelve tribes scattered over here until the time of restoration have to flee their idols, their stubbornness and their disdain for the law, to be that people.

precepts.text: They drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.
precepts.point: Do not get caught up in foolishness. Build yourself up spiritually for the second coming of Christ.

note.label: Destroyed by Familiar Hands

precepts.why:
Our fathers in the wilderness “did all eat the same spiritual meat”, “And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.” What sustained Israel was spiritual, and it was Christ. “But with many of them God was not well pleased”.

That is why Paul says “For though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh”. We walk in the physical, but we do not war after the physical. This is spiritual warfare. “For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds”. Our job is “Casting down imaginations, and every high thing that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God”, casting down every evil imagination in the mind of our people, “and bringing into captivity every thought to the obedience of Christ”, the black Messiah.

So get your mind right and get your mind together, so you can prepare for the second coming of Christ. No matter what happens in this place, do not get caught up in foolishness. If they can treat a white woman like that in Minnesota, imagine how they can treat us. Do not go out there talking about helping march. This is not your problem. Stay in the scripture.

Even your own family in the world, who tell you they hate the Most High, will call and pull you into their stupidity: that's my brother, that's my mama. Do not get caught up. Our job is to get our people ready for the second coming.

precepts.text: All our fathers were under the cloud and drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them, and that Rock was Christ.
precepts.point: Paul confirms it: all our fathers were under the cloud and passed through the sea, and they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them, and that Rock was Christ. The Corinthians Paul wrote were Israelites, for Greece was not even a power on the earth in Moses' day. It was Christ dealing with Israel in the wilderness on behalf of the Most High.

note.label: Exodus 24: The Blood of the Covenant

precepts.why:
Paul confirms who dealt with Israel in the wilderness: “Moreover, brethren, I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea; And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea; And did all eat the same spiritual meat; And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.”

The Corinthians Paul wrote to were Israelites; he says “all our fathers”, and Greece was not even a power on the earth in Moses’ day. It was Christ dealing with Israel in the wilderness on behalf of the Most High. So when the nobles of the children of Israel saw God and did eat and drink, it was Christ, the Rock that followed them, that they saw.

precepts.text: All our fathers were under the cloud and were baptized unto Moses, and that Rock was Christ; the Corinthians were Israelites. Neither be ye idolaters, as it is written, the people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.
precepts.point: Aaron built an altar before it and made proclamation, To morrow is a feast to the LORD; and the people rose up early, offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play. Israel kept provoking God, and the Lord still brought the nation into the promised land as he promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

note.label: Exodus 32: The Golden Calf at Horeb

precepts.why:
Paul writes to the Corinthians: “all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea; And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea”, and “they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.” Our fathers: the Corinthians were Israelites.

“But with many of them God was not well pleased: for they were overthrown in the wilderness. Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted. Neither be ye idolaters, as were some of them; as it is written, The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.” That is the golden calf: Aaron's altar, the feast to the Lord, the burnt offerings and peace offerings, and the people rising up to play.

Israel kept provoking God, and the Lord still brought the nation into the promised land as he promised Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. But the calf is written as our example, so that we do not become idolaters as some of them were.

precepts.text: Neither murmur ye, as some of them also murmured, and were destroyed of the destroyer; now all these things happened unto them for ensamples, and are written for our admonition.
precepts.point: The little ones they said would be a prey, those He would bring into the land; but the children would wander in the wilderness forty years, a year for each of the forty days the land was searched, and bear the whoredoms of their fathers until their carcasses were wasted. The very men that brought up the evil report died by the plague before the Lord, but Joshua and Caleb lived still.

note.label: Numbers 14: The Congregation Rebels and Is Condemned

precepts.why:
“I have heard the murmurings of the children of Israel, which they murmur against me.” For that murmuring the Lord swore, “Your carcases shall fall in this wilderness”, all that were numbered from twenty years old and upward, save Caleb and Joshua; and the men that brought up the evil report “died by the plague before the Lord.”

Paul takes it straight to us: “Neither murmur ye, as some of them also murmured, and were destroyed of the destroyer. Now all these things happened unto them for ensamples: and they are written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come.”

The carcases in the wilderness are an ensample written for our admonition. The same murmuring brings the same destroyer, and we are the ones upon whom the ends of the world are come.

precepts.text: These things happened unto them for ensamples and are written for our admonition; do not be idolaters, fornicators, or tempters of Christ as they were.
precepts.point: These things were our examples, that we should not lust after evil things as they lusted. The people sat down to eat and drink and rose up to play, and that play means sex; that was the golden calf. Neither commit fornication as they did, when three and twenty thousand fell in one day; neither tempt Christ, for it was Christ with us in the wilderness. These things are written for our admonition, that we be warned: idolatry leads to whoredom, spiritual whoredom against the Most High and physical whoredom with it.

note.label: Numbers 25: Baal-peor and the Zeal of Phinehas

precepts.why:
Those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand, and Paul tells us why it is written. “Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted.”

“Neither be ye idolaters, as were some of them; as it is written, The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.” That play means sex; that was the golden calf. “Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them committed, and fell in one day three and twenty thousand.” That is Baal-peor and the daughters of Moab. “Neither let us tempt Christ, as some of them also tempted, and were destroyed of serpents”: it was Christ with us in the wilderness.

“Now all these things happened unto them for ensamples: and they are written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come.” These things are written for our admonition, that we be warned: idolatry leads to whoredom, spiritual whoredom against the Most High and physical whoredom with it.

precepts.text: There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man; God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able, but will with the temptation also make a way to escape.
precepts.point: Far too many tuck and run when the Most High is proving them; he never gives us something we are not able to overcome, and through Israel's schools, classes, and daily teaching he is giving you the way to bear the temptation. Prove to him that you will endure it, love him, and persevere; hard times are the perfect segue back into the vomit you came out of if you do not stand.

note.label: Deuteronomy 8: Keep the Commandments and Live

precepts.why:
“There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.”

The forty years in the wilderness were “to humble thee, and to prove thee, to know what was in thine heart, whether thou wouldest keep his commandments, or no.” Trials and tribulations in this flesh are the Most High proving us the same way, whether a lost spouse, family separating from you, a lost job, or strife with friends.

Far too many tuck and run when the Most High is proving them. He never gives us something we are not able to overcome, and through Israel's schools, classes and daily teaching he is giving you the way to bear the temptation. Prove to him that you will endure it, love him and persevere; hard times are the perfect segue back into the vomit you came out of if you do not stand.

precepts.text: They all drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them, and that Rock was Christ.
precepts.point: David distinguishes the Lord my rock from the God of my rock, just as he says, the Lord said unto my Lord: David understood before anybody else that the head of Christ is God. You have our Rock, and you have the God of our Rock, which is the Father.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
“Of the Rock that begat thee thou art unmindful, and hast forgotten God that formed thee.” Who is that Rock? Paul says of Israel in the wilderness that they “did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.”

Christ did not begin two thousand years after Moses. He was with Israel in the wilderness, the spiritual Rock that followed them, the Rock that begat us. And when it comes to the Rock that created us, we are unmindful.

precepts.text: Let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall, for the Most High provides a way to escape temptation.
precepts.point: Yet Jehu takes no heed to walk in the law of the Most High with all his heart, showing that a man may do great things and still turn away and stay in sin.

note.label: 2 Kings 10: Jehu Destroys Baal and Falls Short of the Law

precepts.why:
“Wherefore let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall.” Jehu stood; he executed judgment on the house of Ahab and destroyed Baal, and the Most High promised his children to the fourth generation would sit on the throne. Still he fell, for he departed not from the sins of Jeroboam.

And there was no excuse: “God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.” The Most High provides a way to escape. Jehu took no heed.

precepts.text: Let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall; no one is above the temptation that took Solomon down.
precepts.point: Because the fathers were not truly in the house, the children learned their mother's tongue and customs instead of Hebrew and the law. Nehemiah contended with them, cursed them, smote certain of them, plucked off their hair, and made them swear not to give or take daughters in marriage with those nations, reminding them that Solomon himself, though beloved of his God, was caused to sin by outlandish women.

note.label: Nehemiah 13: Cleansing the People, the Sabbath, and the Strange Wives

precepts.why:
Solomon, beloved of his God and made king over all Israel, was still caused to sin by outlandish women. Paul's warning follows from that: “Wherefore let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall.”

No one is above the temptation that took Solomon down. The Jews Nehemiah contended with had thought themselves able to marry strange wives without harm, and their children could not even speak the Jews' language. Let him that thinks he stands take heed.

precepts.text: They drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them, and that Rock was Christ.
precepts.point: Only in our affliction do we, many times, consider God and turn our mind and spirit back to the Most High, keeping His laws, statutes, and commandments. Once we start to go off, the Lord will touch us up any way He wants.

note.label: Psalm 78: The History of Israel's Rebellion and the Choosing of Judah and David

precepts.why:
Our fathers “remembered that God was their rock”. Paul tells who that Rock was in the wilderness: they “did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.”

They drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them, and that Rock was Christ. So the rock Israel forgot and remembered again in their affliction is Christ, the same Rock Moses said begat them. When we are slain and return to inquire early after God, it is to that Rock and redeemer that we come back.

precepts.text: That rock that followed them was Christ; the rock of our salvation is Christ.
precepts.point: Why should we make a joyful noise? Because at one time we thought Christ was white, we thought Christ was for everyone, and we were deceived by the nations. Knowing that Christ looked like us and He is a black man from the tribe of Judah is a joyful thing, and He is coming to save us, the so-called black, Hispanic, and native Indians. The rock, our foundation that we build this church and our faith upon, is Christ.

note.label: Psalm 95: The Rock of Our Salvation

precepts.why:
“O come, let us sing unto the Lord: let us make a joyful noise to the rock of our salvation.” Who is the rock of our salvation? Paul says our fathers in the wilderness “did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.”

That rock that followed them was Christ, and the rock of our salvation is Christ. He is the rock, our foundation that we build this church and our faith upon.

Why should we make a joyful noise? Because at one time we thought Christ was white, we thought Christ was for everyone, and we were deceived by the nations. Knowing that Christ looked like us and he is a black man from the tribe of Judah is a joyful thing, and he is coming to save us, the so-called black, Hispanic and native Indians. So we should always be giving praise that you are an Israelite, the best people upon this earth above all nations.

precepts.text: These things were examples so we should not lust, be idolaters, commit fornication, tempt Christ, or murmur as our forefathers did; they are written for our admonition upon whom the ends of the world are come.
precepts.point: When your fathers tempted Me, proved Me, and saw My work. Now we are getting some history of our forefathers, but Paul told us the same thing in the New Testament: do not harden your heart, do not be like our forefathers.

note.label: Psalm 95: The Rock of Our Salvation

precepts.why:
Paul gives the same warning David gives here, and he points to the same forefathers. “Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted.” What our fathers did in the wilderness, when they tempted the Most High and proved him, was written down so that we would not do it.

Paul lists what they did: they were idolaters, for “The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play”; they committed fornication, and “fell in one day three and twenty thousand”; they tempted Christ, “and were destroyed of serpents”; and they murmured, “and were destroyed of the destroyer.” Every one of those is a hardened heart, a mind provoked to sin.

“Now all these things happened unto them for ensamples: and they are written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come.” We are the ones upon whom the ends of the world are come, so the history of our forefathers in Psalm 95 is our admonition: harden not your heart, do not be like them.

precepts.text: Our fathers were all under the cloud and passed through the sea and drank of the spiritual Rock that followed them, and that Rock was Christ, showing the cloud that led us was Christ.
precepts.point: The lesson is that the Most High wants us on one accord, moving when He moves and standing when He stands, just as the powers of heaven do only what He commands.

note.label: Ezekiel 1: The Vision by the River Chebar

precepts.why:
“all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea; And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea”. They “did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.”

The cloud that led us in the wilderness was Christ. That is who the spirit in the chariot is: “the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels”, and the wheels went whithersoever the spirit was to go. Wherever Christ said go, the chariots went, and when He stood still, they stood still.

note.label: The Gospel Is Black Liberation

precepts.why:
Like as I pleaded with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt: we're going back to the same place, and that's what Paul was warning us about. “Moreover, brethren, I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea;” So that proves that the Corinthians were what? Israelites, because Greeks were not with our fathers with Moses. Those are only Israelites. “And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea; And did all eat the same spiritual meat; And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.” So the God of the Old Testament was Christ. That's what Paul is telling you. That was Christ dealing with us in Egypt, when we came out of Egypt. That was Christ, the Son of God.

“But with many of them God was not well pleased: for they were overthrown in the wilderness. Now these things were our examples,” Don't sleep on verse 6. “to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted.” At first glance you make the assumption he's just talking about our people in this time period. He's saying that was our example for a reason, and he's going to say it again. “Neither be ye idolaters, as were some of them; as it is written, The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play. Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them committed, and fell in one day three and twenty thousand. Neither let us tempt Christ, as some of them also tempted, and were destroyed of serpents.” Notice it says neither let us tempt Christ. Remember Numbers 21, about the serpents: everybody goes, "Oh, that was the heavenly Father." No, that was Christ. He's telling you right here. “Neither murmur ye, as some of them also murmured, and were destroyed of the destroyer.”

Here's the point. “Now all these things happened unto them for ensamples:” Ensamples means examples. “and they are written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come.” See that, Paul right there: upon whom the ends of the world are come. Because that generation is this generation. We're going to be back there again.

note.label: When Good Intentions Lead To Bad Judgement In Israel

precepts.why: “But with many of them God was not well pleased: for they were overthrown in the wilderness.” “Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things”. That whole thing happened as an example so we wouldn't lust after evil things as our forefathers did. “Neither be ye idolaters, as were some of them”. They had those calves and were idolatrous. “The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.” Fornication, reveling, idolatry—all type of evil was going on. “Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them committed, and fell in one day three and twenty thousand.” Twenty-three thousand people fell in the wilderness, put to death for that foolishness.

points: They were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea. The baptism is the receiving of the laws and the doing of the laws, in the faith of Christ.
